---
title: "Plain words"
subtitle: "What the terms on this site mean"
---

::: {.glossary}
Bus location (vehicle position)
: Where a bus is, sent from its GPS. Each one also says which trip the bus
  is on, its speed, and how full it is.

Live feed
: The stream of bus locations, arrival predictions and alerts that Island
  Transit publishes for trip-planning apps. It uses a standard format called
  GTFS-Realtime. Each update replaces the last, so nothing is kept unless
  someone saves it.

Collector
: This project's program that asks the feed for its latest data every 20
  seconds and saves exactly what comes back.

Schedule (static GTFS)
: Island Transit's timetable in a standard file format: every trip, every
  stop and every scheduled time.

Trip
: One run of a bus along a route, from its first stop to its last, at a
  scheduled time.

Timepoint
: A stop whose time is printed in Island Transit's timetables. These are the
  times riders are promised, so on-time figures are measured there.

Departure
: The moment a bus leaves a timepoint. At the last stop of a trip, the
  arrival is used instead.

On time
: Leaving no more than 1 minute early and no more than 5 minutes late. At
  the last stop, any early arrival also counts as on time.

Typical departure
: The middle value of how early or late buses left: half left earlier, half
  later (the median).

Seen (observed)
: A departure for which the tracking data was good enough to work out a
  time. Departures that were not seen are reported separately and never
  counted as late.

Service day
: One calendar day in Pacific time. No Island Transit trip crosses midnight.

Coverage
: Whether every scheduled trip shows up in the tracking at all.

Nonresponse
: When data that should be there is missing: a failed request, an empty
  feed, or a gap in a bus's reports.

Measurement error
: When the data is there but wrong: GPS wobble, a bus that seems to jump
  across the map, an old location, or an arrival prediction that misses.

Processing error
: When the data cannot be matched up: a trip in the feed that is not in the
  schedule, or a bus that cannot be tied to a trip.

Paradata
: Data about the data collection itself: every request the collector made,
  how long it took and whether it worked.

Uptime
: The share of 20-second slots in which the collector got a good response.

Arrival prediction
: The "arriving at 3:42" times the feed gives for upcoming stops. This site
  checks them against when the bus actually arrived.

Release
: A download page on GitHub holding one month of files.

Parquet
: A compact file format for tables. Free tools such as Python, R and DuckDB
  open it.
:::

The exact definitions behind every number are on the [Methods](methods.qmd)
page.
